zajjaj:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿إنِّي جَزَيْتُهُمُ اليَوْمَ بِما صَبَرُوا أنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ﴾ — the kasra (reading «إنَّهم») is better, because the kasra carries the meaning "إنِّي جَزَيْتُهم بِما صَبَرُوا" (I have rewarded them for their patience); then He gave a fresh statement and said: "إنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ" (truly they are the triumphant). The fatḥa is good and sound, with the meaning: "إنِّي جَزَيْتُهم لِأنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ" (I have rewarded them because they are the triumphant). There is another possibility in it: the meaning is "جَزَيْتُهُمُ الفَوْزَ" (I have rewarded them with triumph), because the meaning of "أنَّهم هُمُ الفائِزُونَ" is "فَوْزَهم" (their triumph), so the meaning becomes: "جَزَيْتُهم فَوْزَهم" (I have rewarded them with their triumph).

zajjaj:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ في الأرْضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ﴾ — "كَمْ" is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), governed by His saying "لَبِثْتُمْ", and "عَدَدَ سِنِينَ" is accusative (manṣūb) by "كَمْ". It is also permissible to say "كَمْ لَبِتُّمْ في الأرْضِ", with the tāʾ doubled, and the same is permissible in the reply.

zajjaj:113-113.t:
﴿قالُوا لَبِثْنا يَوْمًا أوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ﴾, and "لُبِثْنا" [is also said]. [Translator's note: the source records the form «لُبِثْنا» without further comment.]
His saying: ﴿فاسْألِ العادِّينَ﴾, that is: ask the angels who keep count of how long we remained.

zajjaj:114-114.t: ﴿قالَ إنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إلا قَلِيلا لَوْ أنَّكم كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: "ما لَبِثْتُمْ إلّا قَلِيلًا" (you remained only a little while).

zajjaj:115-115.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنَّكم إلَيْنا لا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾, and "تَرْجِعُونَ" [is also read].

zajjaj:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنَّما حِسابُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ إنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ﴾ — the interpretation is: his reckoning is with his Lord, for indeed the disbelievers will not prosper. The meaning is: "اَلَّذِي لَهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ" (what is due to him with his Lord is that he will not prosper). It is permissible to read "أنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الكافِرُونَ" with fatḥa on "أنَّ". It is also possible that it means "فَأنَّما حِسابُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ فَيُجازِيهِ عَلَيْهِ" (his reckoning is with his Lord, and He will requite him for it), as He said: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّ عَلَيْنا حِسابَهُمْ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 26].

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat "al-Muʾminūn" (The Believers)
Meccan
﷽
From the sura in which the believers are mentioned, His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, i.e. they have attained everlasting continuance in good. Whoever reads "قَدْ أُفْلِحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ" (passive), its meaning is "they have been brought to success". It is narrated from Kaʿb al-Ḥabr that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, created only three things with His hand: He created Ādam ﷺ with His hand, He created the Garden of ʿAdn with His hand, and He wrote the Torah with His hand. Then He said to the Garden of ʿAdn: (Speak), and it said: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, because of the honour it saw in it for its people. "المُؤْمِنُون" are those who affirm the truth of what came from Allah, and that He is One, without partner, and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Prophet.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الوارِثُونَ﴾, i.e. whoever is described by what has preceded — faith and acting upon what is binding on the believer — those are the inheritors.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الفِرْدَوْسَ﴾: it is narrated that Allah, exalted be His praise, appointed for every person a house in Paradise and a house in the Fire. Whoever does the deeds of the people of the Fire, his house in Paradise is inherited by one who did the deeds of the people of Paradise; and whoever does the deeds of the people of Paradise, his house in the Fire is inherited by one who did the deeds of the people of the Fire. "الفِرْدَوْس": its origin is Greek (Rūmī), Arabicised, and it is "the garden (البُسْتان)"; thus it came in the exegesis. It has also been said that the Arabs know (the word) firdaws, and a place with grapevines is called a "firdaws". Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: We have related from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book "Kitāb al-Tafsīr" — which his son ʿAbd Allāh licensed me (to relate) from him — that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, built the Garden of Firdaws with one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and made its mountains of pungent musk. And we have related from someone else that Allah, exalted be His praise, swept the Garden of Firdaws with His hand, and built it with one brick of refined gold and one brick of scattered musk, and planted in it the finest fruit and the finest fragrant plants.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ مِن سُلالَةٍ مِن طِينٍ﴾: "سُلالَة" is on the pattern "فُعالَة". So Allah created Ādam, peace be upon him, from clay.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْناهُ نُطْفَةً﴾: on this view it means the offspring of Ādam. It has also been said: "مِن سُلالَةٍ مِن طِينٍ" means from the semen of Ādam ﷺ. "سُلالَة" is the small amount of what slips out (يَنْسَلّ); everything built on the pattern "فُعالَة" denotes a small amount, such as "الفُضالَة" (leftover), "النُّخالَة" (bran) and "القُلامَة" (nail-parings); its analogy is on this basis.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ خَلَقْنا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنا العَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عِظامًا فَكَسَوْنا العِظامَ لَحْمًا﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 14] is read in four ways. One of them is what we have mentioned; it is also read "فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عَظْمًا فَكَسَوْنا العَظْمَ لَحْمًا"; and it is read "فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عِظامًا فَكَسَوْنا العَظْمَ لَحْمًا"; and it is read "فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عَظْمًا فَكَسَوْنا العِظامَ لَحْمًا". The singular and the plural are both permissible here, because it is known that a human being has bones. When it is mentioned in the singular, that is because it indicates the plural, and because the flesh is with it while its form is singular; so it is known that "العَظْم" is meant as "العِظام". Even stronger than this is permissible in the singular when there is in the speech an indication of the plural. The poet said:
؎فِي حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقَدْ شَجِينا
(In your throat is a bone, and we have choked.)
He means: in your throats are bones.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أنْشَأْناهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 14]: there are three views on it. It has been said: he was made male or female; it has been said: the spirit was breathed into him; and it has been said: hair was made to grow on him. It is narrated «that ʿUmar was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when this verse was revealed, and ʿUmar said: "فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ أحْسَنُ الخالِقِينَ" (So blessed is Allah, the best of creators), and he ﷺ said to ʿUmar: Allah has sealed the verse with it».

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّكم بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ﴾: "لَمائِتُونَ" is possible and "لَمَيْتُونَ" is possible, but the best of them is "لَمَيِّتُونَ", and the reading is on it. "مائِتُونَ" occurs because it is for what is in the future.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا فَوْقَكم سَبْعَ طَرائِقَ﴾ means seven heavens; each one of them is a ṭarīqa (layer). ﴿وَما كُنّا عَنِ الخَلْقِ غافِلِينَ﴾, i.e. We were not such as to neglect guarding them, as He said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا السَّماءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 32]. It is also possible that "وَما كُنّا عَنِ الخَلْقِ غافِلِينَ" means: "it is for Our guarding of them that We created this creation."
﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأسْكَنّاهُ في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 18]: it is narrated that four rivers are from Paradise: the Tigris and the Euphrates, Sayḥān and Jayḥān. The meaning of ﴿فَأسْكَنّاهُ في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 18] is: We made it settled in it, not ceasing.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ هم في صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ﴾: the basic meaning of "الخُشُوع" in the language is submissiveness and humility, and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَخَشَعَتِ الأصْواتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلا تَسْمَعُ إلا هَمْسًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 108]. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: "خاشِعُونَ" means fearful. It is narrated «from the Prophet ﷺ that when he stood in his prayer he would raise his gaze towards the sky; then when ﴿الَّذِينَ هم في صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ﴾ was revealed», he placed his gaze on the place of his prostration.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيْناءَ﴾: "شَجَرَةً" is accusative, conjoined to His saying: ﴿فَأنْشَأْنا لَكم بِهِ جَنّاتٍ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 19], i.e. "and We produced for you by it a tree". It is read "مِن طُورِ سِيناءَ" with fatḥa on the sīn and with kasra on the sīn. "الطُّور" is the mountain. It has been said that "سَيْناء" means stones; and it is — Allah knows best — the name of a place. Whoever says "سَيْناءَ" (with fatḥa) treats it on the pattern of "صَحْراء": it is a diptote. Whoever says "سِيناءَ" with kasra on the sīn — there is nothing in the language on the pattern "فِعْلاء" with the alif being for the feminine, because there is nothing in the language with the feminine alif on the pattern "فِعْلاء"; there are in the language words like "عِلْباء", which is fully declinable (munṣarif). But "سِيناء" here is the name of the area (البُقْعَة), so it is a diptote. His saying: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾: one says "نَبَتَ الشَّجَرُ" and "أنْبَتَ" with one meaning. Zuhayr said:
؎رَأيْتُ ذَوِي الحاجاتِ حَوْلَ بُيُوتِهِمْ .. قَطِينًا لَهم حَتّى إذا أنْبَتَ البَقْلُ
(I saw the needy around their tents, dwelling with them, until when the herbage sprang up.)
The meaning of "تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ" is: it grows with oil in it and oil along with it, as you say "جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ بِالسَّيْفِ", meaning "Zayd came to me with the sword with him". His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَصِبْغٍ لِلآكِلِينَ﴾: by it the olive is meant.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ هو إلا رَجُلٌ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾: "جِنَّة" has the meaning of "جُنُون" (madness); and "الجِنَّة" is also a name for the jinn.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُلْ رَبِّ أنْـزِلْنِي مُنْـزَلا مُبارَكًا﴾: it is read both "مُنْزَلًا" and "مَنزِلًا". "المَنزِل" is a name for every place you alight in, and "المُنْزَل" is the maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "الإنْزال": one says "أنْزَلْتُهُ إنْزالًا، ومُنْزَلًا" (I lodged him, a lodging). "مَنزَلًا" is grammatically possible but has not been read, so do not read it — in the sense of "نَزَلَتْ نُزُولًا، ومَنزَلًا" (I alighted, an alighting).

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾: "اللَّغْو" is all play and jest; and every act of disobedience is cast aside and void (مُلْغاة). They are the ones whom earnestness in what Allah commanded them has kept occupied away from idle talk.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لِلزَّكاةِ فاعِلُونَ﴾: the meaning of "فاعِلُونَ" is "giving (it)".

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ﴾, i.e. they guard their private parts from acts of disobedience.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿إلا عَلى أزْواجِهِمْ أوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُمْ﴾: the position of "ما" is genitive (khafḍ). "عَلى" enters here because the meaning is: "they are blamed for giving free rein to what has been forbidden to them, except with respect to their wives, for they are not blamed for what has been made lawful to them: marrying four, and those whom the right hand possesses." The meaning is: "they are blamed for anything other than their wives and what their right hands possess."

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وراءَ ذَلِكَ﴾, i.e. whoever seeks what is beyond that, ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ﴾: the meaning of "العادُونَ" is the unjust, the wrongdoers, those who have transgressed in wrongdoing.

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم لأماناتِهِمْ﴾ — it is also read "لِأمانَتِهِمْ", singular and plural — ﴿وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ﴾, i.e. they take care to keep their trust and their covenant; they tend (يَرْعَوْنَ) that. The basic meaning of "الرَّعْي" in the language is taking charge of setting right whatever the shepherd (الرّاعِي) is in charge of, in everything. You say: "the imam tends his subjects (رَعِيَّتَهُ)", "the one in charge of the sheep tends his sheep", and "so-and-so tends what is between him and so-and-so", i.e. he takes care to keep right what is between him and the other.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ هم عَلى صَلَواتِهِمْ﴾ — "صَلاتِهِمْ" also; both are read — ﴿يُحافِظُونَ﴾: its meaning is that they perform it at its time. Guarding the prayers is that they are prayed at their times; as for abandoning them, that falls under the chapter of leaving the religion. Those described as guarding are those who observe their times.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أيَعِدُكم أنَّكم إذا مِتُّمْ﴾ — also "مُتُّمْ" — ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ تُرابًا وعِظامًا أنَّكم مُخْرَجُونَ﴾ ﴿هَيْهاتَ هَيْهاتَ لِما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 36]: this is the answer of the chiefs of the people of Thamūd. As for the first "أنَّكم", its position is accusative, in the sense of "does he promise you that (بِأنَّكم) when you die…". The position of the second "أنَّ", according to some, is like the position of the first; it is only mentioned as tawkīd (emphasis). The meaning on this view is: "Does he promise you that you will be brought out when you die?" Since the distance between the first and second "أنَّ" became long through His saying ﴿إذا مِتُّمْ وكُنْتُمْ تُرابًا وعِظامًا﴾, the mention of "أنَّ" was repeated, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ألَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أنَّهُ مَن يُحادِدِ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ فَأنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [al-Tawba: 63], the meaning being "then for him is the fire of Hell". This is according to the doctrine of Sībawayh.
There are two other views about it. The better of them is that the second "أنَّ" together with what it governs is in the position of the nominative, the meaning being: "Does he promise you that you — your being brought out (will be) when you die?" So "أنَّكم مُخْرَجُونَ" is in the sense of "إخْراجُكم" (your being brought out), as though it were said: "Does he promise you that you — your being brought out is at the time of your death and after your death?" What governs "إذا" is then "إخْراجُكم", "إذا" being an adverb of time (ẓarf), and the meaning is: "that you — your being brought out will occur when you die." The third is that what governs "إذا" is "مِتُّمْ", so the meaning is: "that you, whenever you die, your being brought out will occur", so that the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" is implied. The first two views are good. "أيَعِدُكم أنَّكم إذا مِتُّمْ أنَّكم مُخْرَجُونَ" is also grammatically possible, but it has not been read, so do not read it; the meaning of "يَعِدُكم" would then be "he says to you". But it is not permissible in recitation, because recitation is a sunna (a followed practice).

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿هَيْهاتَ هَيْهاتَ لِما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ is read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and with kasra on the tāʾ. "هَيْهاتٍ هَيْهاتٍ" with tanwīn is grammatically possible, and "هَيْهاتًا هَيْهاتًا" is possible. As for fatḥa and kasra without tanwīn, both are frequent in recitation, and the readers and grammarians have mentioned them; it has also been read with kasra and tanwīn. As for tanwīn with fatḥa, I know of no one who read it, so do not read it. As for the fatḥa, the pause is made on a hāʾ: you say "هَيْهاهْ هَيْهاهْ" if you give fatḥa and pause after it; [but when you give kasra] you pause on the tāʾ, whether you were one who uses tanwīn in the base form or one who does not. [Translator's note: the source reads «فَإذا فَتَحْتَ وقَفْتَ عَلى التّاءِ» ("when you give fatḥa you pause on the tāʾ"), which contradicts the preceding sentence; «كَسَرْتَ» (kasra) is evidently intended, and the bracket above supplies it.] Whoever gives it fatḥa — its position being the nominative and its interpretation being "far off is what you are promised (البُعْدُ لِما تُوعَدُونَ)" — does so because it is on a par with sound-words (al-aṣwāt) and is not derived from a verb; so "هَيْهاهْ" was made indeclinable (mabnī), just as "ذَيَّهْ" and "ذِيَّهْ" were made indeclinable. When you give it kasra you make it a plural and make it indeclinable on kasra. Sībawayh said: it is on a par with "عَلْقاة", meaning in its being feminine. Whoever makes it a plural treats it as on a par with the Arabs' saying: "اِسْتَأْصَلَ اللَّهُ عَرْقاتِهِمْ، وعَرْقاتَهم" (may Allah uproot their stock). The one who says "عَرْقاتِهِمْ" with kasra makes it a plural, its singular being as it were "عَرْقَة" and "عَرْق". On this basis the singular of "هَيْهاتَ" — even though it has no singular in actual use — is "هَيْهَة"; this is its implied form even though we do not pronounce it. As for "عَرْقات", its singular is actually spoken: one says "عِرْق", "عَرْقاة", "عَرْقَة" and "عَرْقان". It takes kasra in the plural only because the feminine plural tāʾ takes kasra in place of fatḥa in the plural: you say "مَرَرْتُ بِالهِنْداتِ" and likewise "رَأيْتُ الهِنْداتِ". One also says "أيْهاتَ" in the sense of "هَيْهاتَ"; and one says "هَيْهاتَ ما قُلْتَ" and "هَيْهاتَ لِما قُلْتَ". Whoever says "هَيْهاتَ ما قُلْتَ" means "far off is what you said", and whoever says "هَيْهاتَ لِما قُلْتَ" means "far off is your saying". And they recited:
؎فَأيْهاتَ أيْهاتَ العَقِيقُ ومَن بِهِ ∗∗∗ وأيْهاتَ خِلٌّ بِالعَقِيقِ نُواصِلُهْ
(Far, far off is al-ʿAqīq and those in it, and far off is a friend at al-ʿAqīq with whom we keep company.)
As for whoever gives "هَيْهاتَ" tanwīn, he makes it indefinite, and the meaning is: "a farness (بُعْدٌ) for what you are promised".

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قالَ عَمّا قَلِيلٍ﴾ means "عَنْ قَلِيلٍ" (in a little while), and "ما" is redundant (zāʾida), with the sense of emphasis; it is as though its meaning were: "in a little while they will truly become regretful".

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهم غُثاءً﴾: "الغُثاء" is the perished, worn-out leaves of trees which, when the flood flows, you see mixed with its foam.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا تَتْرى﴾ — it is also read "تَتْرًى" (with tanwīn); "تَتْرِي", without tanwīn, with kasra, is grammatically possible but has not been read, so do not read it. Whoever reads with tanwīn means "وَتْرًا" (one by one): the tāʾ was substituted for the wāw, as they said "تَوْلَج", which is from "وَلَجَ", its base form being "وَوْلَج"; and as the poet said:
؎فَإنْ يَكُنْ أمْسى البِلى تَيْقُورِي
(If decay has become my dignified state…)
i.e. "وَيْقُورِي", which is on the pattern "فَيْعُول" from "الوَقار" (dignity); and as they said "تُجاه", which is really "وُجاه", from "المُواجَهَة" (facing). Whoever says "تَتْرى" without tanwīn makes it on the pattern "فَعْلى" with the feminine alif, so he does not give it tanwīn. The meaning of "تَتْرى" is from "المُواتَرَة". Al-Aṣmaʿī said: the meaning of "واتَرْتُ الخَبَرَ" is "I made parts of the report follow one another, with a short interval between the two reports". Someone else said: "المُواتَرَة" is succession. The origin of all of this is from "الوِتْر", which is "the single": it is that you place each one after its companion, singly, one by one.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وأُمَّهُ آيَةً﴾: He did not say "آيَتَيْنِ" (two signs), because the meaning in the two of them is a single sign. Had "آيَتَيْنِ" been said, it would have been permissible, because there was in each of them what was not in any male or female: Maryam gave birth without a male, and ʿĪsā is a spirit from Allah which He cast into Maryam, and this was never the case in any child.
His saying: ﴿وَآوَيْناهُما إلى رَبْوَةٍ﴾: there are three dialectal forms of "رَبْوَة": "رَبْوَة", "رِبْوَة" and "رُبْوَة", and two other variants: "رَباوَة" and "رِباوَة". According to the lexicographers it is the elevated place. It came in the exegesis that by "رَبْوَة" here is meant Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), that it is the liver (centre) of the earth, and that it is the nearest part of the earth to heaven. It has been said that it means Damascus, and it has been said Palestine and al-Ramla. All of that has come in the exegesis. [Translator's note: the source has «والرَّحْلَة»; the place-name al-Ramla (الرَّمْلَة) is evidently intended.]
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذاتِ قَرارٍ ومَعِينٍ﴾, i.e. having a place of settlement, and "مَعِين" is water flowing from springs. Some of them said it may be on the pattern "فَعِيل" from "المَعْن", derived from "الماعُون". This is far-fetched, because "المَعْن" in the language is a small thing, and "الماعُون" is zakāt, on the pattern "فاعُول" from "المَعْن". Zakāt was named with a small thing only because a quarter of a tenth of property is taken, so it is little out of much. Al-Rāʿī said:
؎قَوْمٌ عَلى التَّنْزِيلِ لَمّا يَمْنَعُوا ∗∗∗ ماعُونَهم ويُبَدِّلُوا التَّنْزِيلا
(A people (holding fast) to the revelation, who have not withheld their zakāt nor altered the revelation.)

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ واعْمَلُوا صالِحًا﴾, i.e. "eat of what is lawful"; every lawful, wholesome food is included in this. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the one addressed by this, and it was said ﴿يا أيُّها الرُّسُلُ﴾, and this address implies that all the messengers were commanded likewise. It is narrated that ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, used to eat from his mother's spinning; and the best of good things is the spoils of war.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ هَذِهِ أُمَّتُكم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً وأنا رَبُّكم فاتَّقُونِ﴾, i.e. "so fear Me for this". We have explained in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ everything that is permissible in the counterpart of this verse. The sum of its interpretation is that your religion is one religion, and that is Islam. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that some people made their religion into several religions, and said: ﴿فَتَقَطَّعُوا أمْرَهم بَيْنَهم زُبُرًا﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 53]. It is also read "زُبَرًا". Whoever reads "زُبُرًا", its interpretation is: "they made their religion into different books" — the plural of "زَبُور" is "زُبُر". Whoever reads "زُبَرًا" means "pieces".

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَذَرْهم في غَمْرَتِهِمْ حَتّى حِينٍ﴾ — "في غَمَراتِهِمْ" is also possible — and its meaning is "in their blindness and their bewilderment". The meaning of "حَتّى حِينٍ" is "until the time when there comes to them the punishment they were promised".

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أيَحْسَبُونَ أنَّما نُمِدُّهم بِهِ مِن مالٍ وبَنِينَ﴾ ﴿نُسارِعُ لَهم في الخَيْراتِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 56] — with nūn — and "يُسارِعُ" with yāʾ, and "يُسارَعُ" as a passive (whose agent is not named). Its interpretation is: "Do they think that Allah's supplying them with wealth and sons is a reward for them?! It is only a gradual leading-on (istidrāj) from Allah." "ما" has the meaning of "الَّذِي": the meaning is "Do they think that that with which We supply them of wealth and sons…", and the khabar (predicate) with it has an omitted element, the meaning being "We hasten for them by it in good things", i.e. "do they think the supply of what We hasten for them by it…". As for whoever reads "يُسارِعُ", it is on two aspects. One of them needs no implied element; the meaning is: "Do they think that Our supplying them hastens for them in good things?!" It may also be in the sense of "Allah hastens for them by it in good things", so that it is like "نُسارِعُ". Whoever reads "يُسارَعُ لَهم في الخَيْراتِ", it is in the sense of "the supply is hastened for them in good things", and in the sense of "We hasten for them in good things", so that (the prepositional phrase) stands in the place of the unnamed agent, with "بِهِ" implied along with it, as we said.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ ما آتَوْا وقُلُوبُهم وجِلَةٌ أنَّهم إلى رَبِّهِمْ راجِعُونَ﴾ — it is also read "يَأْتُونَ ما أتَوْا", with the short vowel; both are good and eloquent. Whoever reads "يُؤْتُونَ ما آتَوْا", its meaning is: "they give what they give while fearing that it will not be accepted from them; their hearts are fearful because they will return to their Lord", i.e. because they are certain that they will return to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Whoever reads "يَأْتُونَ ما أتَوْا" means: "they do of good deeds what they do while their hearts are fearful, fearing that despite their striving they are falling short".

zajjaj:61-61.t:
﴿أُولَئِكَ يُسارِعُونَ في الخَيْراتِ﴾: "يُسْرِعُونَ في الخَيْراتِ" is also possible, and its meaning is the meaning of "يُسارِعُونَ". One says "أسْرَعْتُ" and "سارَعْتُ" with one meaning, except that "سارَعْتُ" is more intensive than "أسْرَعْتُ".
His saying: ﴿وَهم لَها سابِقُونَ﴾: there are two aspects in it. One is that its meaning is "they are foremost towards them (إلَيْها)", as He said: ﴿بِأنَّ رَبَّكَ أوْحى لَها﴾ [al-Zalzala: 5], i.e. "He revealed to it (إلَيْها)". It may also be "وَهم لَها سابِقُونَ" meaning "for the sake of acquiring them", as you say "I honour so-and-so for you (لَكَ)", i.e. for your sake.

zajjaj:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إلا وُسْعَها﴾: "وَلا يُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إلّا وُسْعَها" is grammatically possible, but it has not been read; had it been read, the nūn would still be better, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَدَيْنا كِتابٌ يَنْطِقُ بِالحَقِّ﴾.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ قُلُوبُهم في غَمْرَةٍ مِن هَذا﴾: "هَذا" may be a reference to the pious deeds described in His saying ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ هم مِن خَشْيَةِ رَبِّهِمْ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 57] up to His saying ﴿يُسارِعُونَ في الخَيْراتِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 61], i.e. "the hearts of these are in blindness regarding this". "هَذا" may also be a reference to the Book, the meaning being: "rather their hearts are in heedlessness regarding the Book which speaks the truth", in which their deeds are counted. His saying: ﴿وَلَهم أعْمالٌ مِن دُونِ ذَلِكَ هم لَها عامِلُونَ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, told of what would happen among them, and made known that they would do deeds that distance one from Allah, other than the deeds with which they were mentioned.

zajjaj:64-64.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتّى إذا أخَذْنا مُتْرَفِيهِمْ بِالعَذابِ إذا هم يَجْأرُونَ﴾, i.e. they cry out loudly. The punishment with which they were seized was the sword. One says "جَأرَ، يَجْأرُ، جُؤارًا" when one cries out.

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿تَنْكِصُونَ﴾, i.e. you turn back.

zajjaj:67-67.t:
His saying: ﴿مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ بِهِ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). His saying "بِهِ", i.e. by the Sacred House: they say "the House is ours".
His saying: ﴿سامِرًا﴾ has the meaning of "سُمَّرًا" (people conversing at night); "سُمّارًا" is also possible. "السّامِر" is the group who converse at night. They were called "سُمّار" only from "السَّمَر", which is the shade of the moon; likewise "السُّمْرَة" (brownness) is derived from this.
His saying: ﴿تَهْجُرُونَ﴾, i.e. you abandon the Qurʾān. "تَهْجِرُونَ" is also possible: you talk nonsense. It has also been read "تُهْجِرُونَ", i.e. you speak obscenity (الهُجْر); and it has been said: they used to revile the Prophet ﷺ. It is also possible that the hāʾ (in بِهِ) refers to the Book, the meaning being: "you used to turn back on your heels, being arrogant on account of the Book", i.e. arrogance arises in you by its being recited to you. "تَنْكَصُونَ" is also grammatically possible, but I know of no one who read it.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوِ اتَّبَعَ الحَقُّ أهْواءَهُمْ﴾: it came in the exegesis that "الحَقّ" is Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. It is also possible that "الحَقّ", the first, in His saying ﴿بَلْ جاءَهم بِالحَقِّ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 70], is the revelation, i.e. with the revelation which is the truth; and the interpretation of "وَلَوِ اتَّبَعَ الحَقُّ أهْواءَهم" is then: "if the revelation were according to what they like, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted".
His saying: ﴿بَلْ أتَيْناهم بِذِكْرِهِمْ﴾, i.e. with that in which is their glory and their honour. It may also be "بِذِكْرِهِمْ", i.e. with the Reminder in which there is a share for them, if they followed it.

zajjaj:100-100.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن ورائِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ إلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾: "يَوْمِ" is muḍāf (annexed) to "يُبْعَثُونَ", because nouns of time are annexed to verbs. "البَرْزَخ" in the language is a barrier, and here it is what lies between the death of the dead person and his resurrection.

zajjaj:101-101.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَإذا نُفِخَ في الصُّورِ فَلا أنْسابَ بَيْنَهم يَوْمَئِذٍ ولا يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾: it has been said this is at the first blowing, and it may be after the second blowing. As for "الصُّور", it came in the exegesis that it is a horn which is blown into, and people are resurrected at the second blowing. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخْرى فَإذا هم قِيامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 68]. Many of the lexicographers said: "الصُّور" is the plural of "صُورَة" (form). But what has come in the language as the plural of "صُورَة" is "صُوَر", and so it came in the Qurʾān: ﴿وَصَوَّرَكم فَأحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 3], and no one read "فَأحْسَنَ صُورَكم". Moreover, if it were the plural of "صُورَة", He would also have said "ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيها أُخْرى" (feminine), because you say "هَذِهِ صُوَرٌ" and you do not say "هَذا صُوَرٌ" except weakly. So it is according to what came in the exegesis.
As for His saying ﴿وَلا يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ — while He said in another place ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24], and in another place ﴿وَأقْبَلَ بَعْضُهم عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 27] — someone may ask: how is it that "وَلا يَتَساءَلُونَ" (they will not ask one another) occurs and "وَأقْبَلَ بَعْضُهم عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ" (they will turn to one another, asking) occurs? (The answer is that) the Day of Resurrection is fifty thousand years in length, so in it there are periods and states. "يَوْمَئِذٍ" (on that day) is said only as you say: "We are today (اليَوْمَ) doing such-and-such", and you do not mean by it "on this day of yours"; you only mean "we in this time". So "يَوْم" applies to a stretch of time. As for ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ ولا جانٌّ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 39], no one is asked about his sin in order to obtain information — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, already knows what they did before. As for His saying ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24], they are asked a question of rebuke, not a question seeking information, as He said: ﴿وَإذا المَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 8] ﴿بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 9] — she is asked only to rebuke the one who killed her. Likewise His saying: ﴿أأنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116]. So what is asked about on the Day of Resurrection is for making (them) confess and for rebuke; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, already knows what has been, and has counted its great and its small.

zajjaj:104-104.t: His saying: ﴿تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ النّارُ﴾: "يَلْفَحُ" and "يَنْفَحُ" have one meaning, except that lafḥ (scorching) has a greater effect. ﴿وَهم فِيها كالِحُونَ﴾: "الكالِح" is one whose lip has drawn back from his teeth, like what you see of sheep's heads when the fire touches them: the teeth stand out and the lips draw back.

zajjaj:106-106.t: ﴿قالُوا رَبَّنا غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنا شِقْوَتُنا﴾ — it is also read "شَقاوَتُنا", and the meaning is the same. ﴿وَكُنّا قَوْمًا ضالِّينَ﴾: they confessed that.

zajjaj:108-108.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ اخْسَئُوا فِيها ولا تُكَلِّمُونِ﴾: the meaning of "اخْسَؤُوا" is: get far away, the going-away of those under (divine) wrath. One says "خَسَأْتُ الكَلْبَ، أخْسَؤُهُ" when you drive the dog away so that it goes off.

zajjaj:110-110.t:
His saying: ﴿فاتَّخَذْتُمُوهم سِخْرِيًّا﴾: the best is to assimilate the dāl into the tāʾ, because the two points of articulation are close; and if you wish you may pronounce it distinctly, because the dāl is from one word and the tāʾ from another, and between the dāl and the tāʾ in articulation there is some distance. The dhāl is not to the tāʾ as the dāl is to the tāʾ: the tāʾ and the ṭāʾ are from one place, from the roots of the upper front teeth and the tip of the tongue, while the dhāl is from the edges of the upper front teeth and just short of the tip of the tongue. [Translator's note: the word in the verse has a dhāl (اتَّخَذْتُمُوهُمْ); the source speaks of "dāl" in the first two places, apparently meaning the dhāl, and then distinguishes dhāl from dāl. Translated as written.]
His saying: ﴿سِخْرِيًّا﴾ is read with ḍamma and kasra, and both are good, except that they said that some of the lexicographers said: what is from mockery is with kasra, and what is from the sense of subjection (taskhīr) is with ḍamma. According to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl both are one; and kasra, to harmonise with the (following) kasra, is better.

zajjaj:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿أمْ تَسْألُهم خَرْجًا فَخَراجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ﴾, i.e. "or do you ask them for a wage for what you have brought them?" It is also read "خِراجًا فَخَراجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ", and "خَراجًا فَخَراجُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ" is grammatically possible. [Translator's note: the variant is printed «خِراجًا» with kasra in the source; translated as written.]

zajjaj:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿لَناكِبُونَ﴾ means: surely turning away from the right course.

zajjaj:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أخَذْناهم بِالعَذابِ فَما اسْتَكانُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ وما يَتَضَرَّعُونَ﴾, i.e. "they did not humble themselves"; and what they were seized with was hunger.

zajjaj:77-77.t: ﴿حَتّى إذا فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ بابًا ذا عَذابٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾: it has been said: the sword and killing. ﴿إذا هم فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾: "المُبْلِس" is the one who falls silent in bewilderment.

zajjaj:84-84.t: ﴿قُلْ لِمَنِ الأرْضُ ومَن فِيها إنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 85]: about this "لِلَّهِ" there is no disagreement among the Readers; had it been read "اللَّهُ", it would have been good. As for the two after it, the reading in them is "سَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ" and "لِلَّهِ". Whoever reads "سَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ" takes it as the answer to the question: when he says "مَن رَبُّ السَّماواتِ السَّبْعِ" (Who is the Lord of the seven heavens?), the answer is "اللَّهُ" (Allah); and that is the reading of the people of Basra. Whoever reads "لِلَّهِ", that is also good: if it were said "Who is the owner of this house?" and the answer were "Zayd", this would be an answer according to the wording of the question; and if you said, in answer to "Who is the owner of this house?", "لِزَيْدٍ" (Zayd's), it would be permissible, because the meaning of "Who is the owner of this house?" is "Whose is this house (لِمَن هَذِهِ الدّارُ)?".

zajjaj:88-88.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ يُجِيرُ ولا يُجارُ عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. "He grants protection from His punishment, and no one can grant protection against Him from His punishment"; likewise "He grants protection from (the harm of) His creation, and no one can grant protection against Him."

zajjaj:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿فَأنّى تُسْحَرُونَ﴾: the meaning of "تُسْحَرُونَ" and "تُؤْفَكُونَ" is: you are turned away from the right course and from the truth.

zajjaj:91-91.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إذًا لَذَهَبَ كُلُّ إلَهٍ بِما خَلَقَ ولَعَلا بَعْضُهم عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾, i.e. some of them would seek to overpower others. ﴿سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ﴾ means: "declaring Allah transcendent and free of all evil, and of there being any god other than Him — exalted is He above that, greatly exalted."

zajjaj:93-93.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ رَبِّ إمّا تُرِيَنِّي ما يُوعَدُونَ﴾ ﴿رَبِّ فَلا تَجْعَلْنِي في القَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 94]: the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition — the condition of requital — and it (the vocative "رَبِّ") is a parenthesis between the condition and the requital. The meaning is: "If You show me what they are promised, then do not, O my Lord, place me among the wrongdoing people", i.e. "if vengeance comes down upon them, O Lord, then put me outside of them". "فَلا تَجْعَلَنِّي" is grammatically possible, but it has not been read.

zajjaj:97-97.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُلْ رَبِّ أعُوذُ بِكَ مِن هَمَزاتِ الشَّياطِينِ﴾: the singular of "الهَمَزات" is "هَمْزَة", and it is the touch of Satan. It may also mean "the promptings (نَزَغات) of Satan"; the prompting (نَزْغ) of Satan is his whispering until he diverts one from the command of Allah the Exalted.

zajjaj:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿وَأعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أنْ يَحْضُرُونِ﴾: "وَأعُوذُ بِكَ رَبُّ أنْ يَحْضُرُونِ" is grammatically possible but has not been read, so do not read it; "وَأعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّي أنْ يَحْضُرُونِ" is possible, and "رَبِّيَ" is possible. These are four ways, but it should only be read in one, which is what people follow: "رَبِّ", with kasra on the bāʾ and dropping the yāʾ. The yāʾ was dropped because of the vocative, the meaning being "and I seek refuge in You, O my Lord". Whoever says "رَبُّ" with ḍamma takes it in the sense of "O Lord (يا أيُّها الرَّبُّ)"; and whoever says "رَبِّي" follows the base form, as He said: "يا عِبادِي فاتَّقُونِ".

zajjaj:99-99.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَ أحَدَهُمُ المَوْتُ﴾ means those who were mentioned before this place and who rejected the resurrection. He made known that when death comes to one of them, ﴿قالَ رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ﴾ ﴿لَعَلِّي أعْمَلُ صالِحًا فِيما تَرَكْتُ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 100]. His saying "ارْجِعُونِ" (plural) while he means Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, alone: the address in the request came in the form (used in) His statements about Himself, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي ونُمِيتُ﴾ [Qāf: 43], while He alone gives life and causes death. This is an expression the Arabs know for one of great standing: he speaks of himself in the way a group speaks of itself. So likewise the address came in "ارْجِعُونِ".
His saying: ﴿كَلا﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 100] is a rebuke and a warning.
